chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who performed 'Umrah with Hajj (Tamattu'), entered Mecca, performed Tawaf and Sa'i, put on his clothes, and became free from Ihram, but forgot to shorten his prayer until he went out to Arafat. He said: 'There is no harm with him; he completes based on the 'Umrah and its Tawaf, and the Tawaf of Hajj follows after it.'

key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat (the plain where the standing of Hajj occurs)
key_terms.وَأَحَلَّ: Ihram (state of freedom from ritual consecration)
key_terms.يُقَصِّرَ: Qasr (shortening the four-rak'ah prayer to two)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim in Tamattu' forgets to shorten prayers after 'Umrah Tawaf?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the juristic principle of *al-asl fi al-af'al al-ibahah* (the default permissibility of actions) is applied to the Hajj rituals, confirming that forgetting to shorten prayers after exiting Ihram for 'Umrah does not invalidate the transition to Hajj. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on ease and the non-penalty for unintentional omissions during the sacred rites, as the pilgrim proceeds directly to Arafat with the 'Umrah Tawaf remaining valid.
